root_cause.text: The networking recvmsg callee paths incorrectly treated `msg_get_inq` as an output flag and wrote to it inside `tcp_recvmsg_locked`/`unix_stream_read_generic`, causing a NULL dereference in AF_UNIX splice when `state->msg`/`msg` can be NULL and violating the caller-owned input semantics of `struct msghdr`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `msg->msg_get_inq = 1` from both `net/ipv4/tcp.c` and `net/unix/af_unix.c`, and the commit message explicitly states "`msg_get_inq` is an input field from caller to callee. Don't set it in the callee" and "avoid NULL pointer dereference in `unix_stream_read_generic` if `state->msg` is NULL ... A NULL `state->msg` can happen when splicing."

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The networking recvmsg callee paths incorrectly treated `msg_get_inq` as an output flag and wrote to it inside `tcp_recvmsg_locked`/`unix_stream_read_generic`, causing a NULL dereference in AF_UNIX splice when `state->msg`/`msg` can be NULL and violating the caller-owned input semantics of `struct msghdr`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `msg->msg_get_inq = 1` from both `net/ipv4/tcp.c` and `net/unix/af_unix.c`, and the commit message explicitly states "`msg_get_inq` is an input field from caller to callee. Don't set it in the callee" and "avoid NULL pointer dereference in `unix_stream_read_generic` if `state->msg` is NULL ... A NULL `state->msg` can happen when splicing."

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop setting `msg->msg_get_inq` in `tcp_recvmsg_locked()` while preserving the TCP inq cmsg flag to correct recvmsg inq handling.
intent_record.what: The conditional block guarded by `if (tp->recvmsg_inq)` was reduced from three statements to one by keeping only `*cmsg_flags = TCP_CMSG_INQ;` under the condition and removing the assignment `msg->msg_get_inq = 1;`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when `tp->recvmsg_inq` is enabled, the code still sets the TCP inq control-message flag but no longer marks the message header with `msg->msg_get_inq = 1`, changing recvmsg behavior so the inq state is advertised only through `cmsg_flags` and preventing the extra per-message inq flag from being set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix tcp_recvmsg() to process TCP INQ state when the TCP_CMSG_INQ flag is present, not just when msg_get_inq is requested.
intent_record.what: The patch changes two conditional expressions in tcp_recvmsg(): it replaces the top-level logical OR `(cmsg_flags || msg->msg_get_inq)` with a bitwise OR `(cmsg_flags | msg->msg_get_inq)`, and it broadens the inner condition from checking only `msg->msg_get_inq` to checking `(cmsg_flags & TCP_CMSG_INQ) | msg->msg_get_inq` before computing `msg->msg_inq` and possibly emitting the TCP_CM_INQ control message.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now enters the ancillary-data handling block whenever any cmsg flag bit is set or `msg_get_inq` is requested, and it computes the INQ hint not only when the caller explicitly requested `msg_get_inq` but also when the TCP_CMSG_INQ control-message flag is set. This fixes a case where TCP INQ control-message handling could skip populating `msg_inq` and related cmsg data unless `msg_get_inq` was separately enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from `unix_stream_read_generic` without changing runtime behavior.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `bool do_cmsg;` was removed from `unix_stream_read_generic`, while the surrounding declarations and code shown remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this has no direct behavioral effect unless the variable was unused; removing the declaration eliminates an unused local variable and may silence compiler warnings without changing execution logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature recvmsg inq setup in `unix_stream_read_generic()` to avoid incorrect stream read ancillary-state handling.
intent_record.what: The code removes the early assignment of `do_cmsg = READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq);` and the conditional `if (do_cmsg) msg->msg_get_inq = 1;` from `unix_stream_read_generic()` immediately after obtaining `u = unix_sk(sk);`.
intent_record.how: This stops the function from unconditionally snapshotting `recvmsg_inq` and setting `msg->msg_get_inq` at that earlier point, so the inq control-message handling is no longer enabled there and must be deferred or handled elsewhere in the function, avoiding premature or incorrect setup during stream reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix unix stream receive handling so in-queue length is reported whenever `recvmsg_inq`-driven `SCM_INQ` control data is enabled, not just when `msg_get_inq` is requested.
intent_record.what: The change introduces a new local boolean variable `do_cmsg` initialized from `READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq)` before calling `scm_recv_unix()`, and changes the subsequent condition from `if (msg->msg_get_inq && (copied ?: err) >= 0)` to `if ((do_cmsg | msg->msg_get_inq) && (copied ?: err) >= 0)`, while reusing `do_cmsg` inside the block to decide whether to emit the `SCM_INQ` control message.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now enters the `msg_inq` update block not only when the caller explicitly requested `msg_get_inq`, but also when the socket's `recvmsg_inq` setting is enabled, ensuring `msg->msg_inq` is populated whenever ancillary `SCM_INQ` data may be generated. This fixes previously missing in-queue length reporting for the `recvmsg_inq` path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix unix stream receive handling so in-queue length is reported whenever `recvmsg_inq`-driven `SCM_INQ` control data is enabled, not just when `msg_get_inq` is requested.
Remove an unused local variable from `unix_stream_read_generic` without changing runtime behavior.
Remove premature recvmsg inq setup in `unix_stream_read_generic()` to avoid incorrect stream read ancillary-state handling.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix socket receive-path in-queue reporting so INQ/SCM_INQ control data is generated based on the protocol cmsg INQ flag rather than only the msg_get_inq request bit.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly stop recv paths from treating `msg_get_inq` as a callee-written/output field and switch INQ/SCM_INQ reporting to protocol/cmsg state, which matches the root cause involving improper writes to `msg_get_inq` and NULL dereference risk when `msg` can be NULL.

The change only removes an unused local variable in `unix_stream_read_generic` and does not affect `msg_get_inq` handling, NULL `msg` dereference behavior, or recvmsg caller/callee semantics related to the vulnerability.

The change removes recvmsg inq handling from `unix_stream_read_generic()`, which is one of the exact callee paths implicated in the root cause for incorrectly treating `msg_get_inq` as callee-written state. That directly relates to preventing the bad ancillary-state/write behavior that could occur when `msg` is NULL.

candidates.rationale: This directly implements the root cause by treating msg_get_inq as callee-owned output state and writing into struct msghdr from tcp_recvmsg_locked(), which is invalid when the caller semantics make it an input flag and can be unsafe if msg is absent in some recv paths.

This is the AF_UNIX-side direct bug: unix_stream_read_generic() writes to msg_get_inq as if it were an output field. In splice-related paths msg can be NULL, so this assignment can NULL-dereference and also violates caller-owned msghdr semantics.

This statement gates INQ reporting on msg_get_inq, reflecting the incorrect design that relies on the callee-mutated request bit instead of protocol cmsg state. It is part of the vulnerable behavior tied to the bad write and wrong semantics.

This condition incorrectly depends on msg_get_inq for receive-path INQ handling, reinforcing the misuse of msg_get_inq as mutable state rather than a caller input and contributing to the flawed recvmsg behavior.
This line is part of the incorrect logic that uses msg_get_inq as the trigger for in-queue reporting after the callee may have modified it, instead of relying solely on protocol-managed cmsg flags.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct AF_UNIX bug described in the root cause: the callee writes to msg_get_inq as if it were output state. In splice-related paths the msg pointer can be NULL, so this assignment can NULL-dereference and also violates the caller-owned input semantics of struct msghdr.

This statement is the TCP-side manifestation of the same root cause: tcp_recvmsg_locked() mutates msg_get_inq as though it were callee-owned output state, instead of treating it as a caller-provided input flag in struct msghdr.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact introduction of the new msg_get_inq/msg_inq handling in the vulnerable path. The vulnerable construct is present in tcp_recvmsg_locked(): `if (tp->recvmsg_inq) { *cmsg_flags = TCP_CMSG_INQ; msg->msg_get_inq = 1; }`. This writes to `msg->msg_get_inq` inside the recvmsg callee, treating it as an output/control flag instead of caller-owned input state. The root cause says recvmsg callees must not set `msg_get_inq` themselves, and doing so is unsafe when `msg` may be NULL in some call paths. The commit also adds in tcp_recvmsg(): `if ((cmsg_flags || msg->msg_get_inq) && ret >= 0) { ... if (msg->msg_get_inq) { msg->msg_inq = tcp_inq_hint(sk); ... } }`, which further relies on callee-side mutation of `msg_get_inq` and writes `msg->msg_inq`. There is no protective check here establishing that `msg` is always non-NULL in all callers, and more importantly the semantics are wrong because `msg_get_inq` is being set by the callee. Therefore the buggy construct is introduced here. The fix is not present because the code still contains the callee-side assignment `msg->msg_get_inq = 1;` rather than only reading a caller-provided flag.
